title: Indian Suite
why: web: (not flagged verify) Indian Suite (The Snake Charmer, Juggernaut, Indian Serenade, Dancing Girls; Schott London 1922, plate 30802, ded. Marjorie Forsyth Barlow) is a PIANO suite: IMSLP lists Instrumentation = piano (the 'vn pf' tag looks like an error), and it appears neither on the composer's violin & piano page nor in Schott's violin listing.

title: Menuet-Pompadour, Op. 119
why: web: (not flagged verify, low confidence) IMSLP's Godard work list gives Op. 119 'Menuet-Pompadour' as a song for voice and piano (text by J.-B. Rousseau), with a violin & piano version noted alongside. The only violin edition found is an unattributed anthology print, Les Perles du Violoniste II,27 (Warsaw: Gebethner & Wolff, plate G2968W, n.d., ed. Maurice Rosen). So it is an obscure transcription of a song, not a documented violin original; keep it out unless you want such prints. If kept, house style would be 'Menuet-Pompadour, Op. 119 (orig. voice)'.

title: Concerto in D minor, Op. 29
why: web: (not flagged verify) Violin Concerto in D minor, Op. 29 is UNPUBLISHED: IMSLP only has a holograph manuscript (n.d., ca. 1870), 'Extra Information: unpublished', and notes that Godard seems not to have orchestrated it himself (orchestration by Martin Yates released on a 2022 Dutton CD). No published edition, so out of scope; the published concertos are Op. 35 (already listed) and Op. 131 (N13).

title: Scènes écossaises, Op. 138
why: web: Scènes écossaises, Op. 138 is an OBOE work: IMSLP gives 'oboe, orchestra' (1892; Hamelle, Paris, 1893, plates J. 3595-97 H; dedicated to Georges Gillet), 3 pieces (Légende pastorale, Sérénade à Mabel, Marche des Highlanders), with oboe & piano arrangements (Hamelle 1892) and later oboe (or flute) & piano editions (Southern, Accolade, Ludwig; Kalmus reprints the orchestral material). No violin version is listed on IMSLP or in any publisher listing found; the 'oboe or violin' evidence in the draft is unsupported.

title: Air varié No. 7 in E major
why: web: IMSLP lists only 1834 autograph manuscripts (full score, piano score, violin part; "first publication 2025" = scan upload); no printed edition and not in the Wikipedia work list. Juvenile manuscript-only piece.

title: Variations on a Theme from Bellini's 'Norma' in G major, Op. 2
why: web: IMSLP lists only 1834 autograph manuscripts (family archive, scans uploaded 2026; "first publication 2021"); no printed edition. Early manuscript-only work, so out of scope.

title: Sonata in D major
why: web: The work exists (Hudec 199, Sonata in D major for violin and piano, 1875 per Wikipedia / 1876 per some CD booklets; recorded by Josef Suk and Josef Hala, Supraphon SU 3473-2, 2000) but I found NO published edition: it is not on IMSLP and no Barenreiter/Supraphon/Panton/CHF score turned up, so treat as unpublished/manuscript. (Also a lost/unpublished Sonata in C major, H 193, 1874.) If the owner decides to admit recorded-but-unpublished works, the title would be 'Sonata in D major' with no opus number.

title: Bagatelle (1917)
why: web: The piece exists but not as queued: it is Bagatela 'S kyticí v ruce' ('With Nosegay in Hand'), 1917, publ. Hudební matice, Prague 1923 (H.M. 294), scored for flute, violin and piano (IMSLP also lists a 2 violins + piano alternative) - i.e. a chamber trio, not a violin solo/duo work. 'Bagatelle (1917)' is not a title in any source. If the owner still wants it, use title "Bagatelle 'S kyticí v ruce'", accompaniment '2 violins & piano', category 'Duet / Double Concerto', ~2 min, low level.

why: web: No published violin & piano edition found. IMSLP's Gavotte (1885, dedicated to Dr C.W. Buck) lists only an orchestral arrangement (A. Schmid, Schott), a string-orchestra arrangement (J. why: web: Manuscript-only: Reminiscences (1877, D major, inscribed to Oswin Grainger) survives in BL Add. MS 57912; Wikipedia marks it 'manuscript'; the only score on IMSLP is an amateur typeset by John Morrison (2019).

title: Study for Strengthening the Third Finger
why: web: Manuscript-only one-page exercise ('Exercise for the 3rd finger', written 1877, copied for Heifetz in 1920); only an amateur typeset (J. Morrison, 2019) on IMSLP; not a repertoire piece.

title: Very Easy Melodious Exercises in the First Position, Op. 22
why: web: Very easy first-position teaching exercises (Op. 22, 1892) - below the catalogue's grade 3-4 entry level and method-book material, although the work exists (IMSLP/Wikipedia).

title: Concert Piece No. 2, Op. 15 No. 2
why: web: "Concert Piece No. 2" is a placeholder; the piece is "Maggiolata" (Chant de mai), published by Hamelle for viola or cello & piano (IMSLP; Hubay Foundation scoring "va/vc-pf/orch"). No violin edition found.

title: Graded Course of Violin Playing (8 books)
why: web: Pedagogical method book (Graded Course of Violin Playing, 8 books), not a repertoire work; category 'Technique & Scales' is not a catalogue category and Auer's Graded Course is out of scope. Gap check for Auer's own pieces found nothing new: IMSLP's Auer page lists exactly six compositions (Op. 2 Tarantelle de concert, Op. 3 Reverie, Op. 4 Romance, Op. 5 Rhapsodie hongroise, Reverie No. 2, Op. 9 12 Characteristic Preludes) and ru.wikipedia's list of Auer's original compositions agrees (Opp. 2, 3, 4, 5, 9 plus Reverie No. 2, no opus; Op. 9 is for solo violin, publ. 1926). No Op. 1, 6, 7 or 8 of his own exists in either source; all six are already in existing/queued (N1-N3 left as drafted).

title: Barcarolle in F minor, Op. 6
why: web: IMSLP offers only a 2026 modern typeset (Scott Eisfeldt, CC BY-SA) of the 1902 holograph held in the National Library of Israel; no historical or publisher edition, and it is not in the IMSLP list of works as published. Unpublished early work. (Owner may keep it if IMSLP typesets count as editions.)

title: Souvenir de Saint-Pétersbourg in G major (Caprice sur des motifs russes)

title: Valse mélancolique in B minor, Op. 11
why: web: Op. 11 (1902-06): IMSLP offers only a 2026 modern typeset (Scott Eisfeldt) of the manuscript in the National Library of Israel; the IMSLP list also marks it "manuscript". No historical or publisher edition; unpublished early work.

title: Romanza
why: web: A Romanza for violin & piano is listed in Granados work lists (en/ca Wikipedia: undated; a recording by Kiesewetter/Riva is on MusicBrainz) but I found no published edition: the claimed UME late-20th-c. first edition is unconfirmed, it is not on IMSLP, and the 8-minute length looks wrong for a Romanza. Re-add only if a publisher/edition can be named. Other undated violin & piano items in the same lists (Melodía 1903, Tres preludios: La góndola / El toque de guerra / Elevación; Serenata for 2 violins & piano 1914, incomplete) also have no edition evidence, so not offered as gaps.

title: Sonata in G minor, BWV 1020
why: web: Spurious for J. S. Bach: IMSLP files it under C. P. E. Bach (H. 542.5, Wq deest; 'formerly catalogued as BWV 1020'); Wikipedia chamber list: 'now attributed to C. P. E. Bach'. Henle HN 458 prints it only as an appendix after BWV 1021/1023. If the owner wants it anyway: 'Sonata in G minor, H. 542.5 (formerly BWV 1020)', violin (or flute) & harpsichord, Henle HN 458 (ed. Eppstein, 1990).

title: Trio Sonata in C major, BWV 1037
why: web: Spurious for J. S. Bach: IMSLP files it under Johann Gottlieb Goldberg (Trio Sonata in C major, DurG 13; 'formerly attributed to J. S. Bach as BWV 1037'); Wikipedia chamber list: 'now attributed to Goldberg'. Printed under Bach's name only in older editions (BGA 9, 1860; Crussard, Foetisch 1948).

title: Trio Sonata in D minor, BWV 1036
why: web: Spurious for J. S. Bach: it is C. P. E. Bach's Trio Sonata in D minor H. 569 / Wq 145 (1731, rev. 1747), scored for FLUTE, violin and continuo per IMSLP (not 2 violins); an earlier version is a violin & harpsichord sonata. Wikipedia chamber list: 'now attributed to C. P. E. Bach'.

title: Sonata in G major, HWV 363a
why: web: Not a Handel violin sonata: HWV 363a is the oboe sonata in F major and HWV 363b the flute sonata in G major (Op. 1 No. 5; mvts Adagio-Allegro-Adagio-Bourree-Menuet). IMSLP's 'Violin Sonata in G major, HWV 363a' page only carries a Creative-Commons typeset violin version (Reely / A. Sievers); it is absent from the Barenreiter Complete Works for Violin & Basso Continuo, so there is no published violin edition. (verify:false entry, flagged because of the error.)
